territorial_scope.description: Open for signature by Council of Europe member States, non-member States that participated in its elaboration, and the European Union; applies to each Party's activities within the lifecycle of AI systems.

evidence.provision: Article 30 - Signature and entry into force, para. 1
evidence.quote: This Convention shall be open for signature by the member States of the Council of Europe, the non-member States which have participated in its elaboration and the European Union.

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Council of Europe treaty requiring Parties to adopt or maintain measures so AI system lifecycle activities are consistent with human rights, democracy and the rule of law. Covers public authorities and, by declaration, private actors; excludes national security and defence. Opened for signature at Vilnius, 5 September 2024.
summary.long: Each Party must adopt or maintain measures so that activities within the lifecycle of AI systems are consistent with human rights, democracy and the rule of law, graduated by the severity and probability of adverse impacts (Arts. 1-2). Obligations cover public authorities and, via declarations, private actors (Art. 3(1)). Chapter II addresses human rights and democratic processes (Arts. 4-5). Chapter III covers human dignity, transparency and oversight, accountability, non-discrimination, privacy, reliability and controlled testing environments (Arts. 7-13). Chapter IV requires remedies, information allowing persons to contest decisions made or substantially informed by AI systems, complaint routes, procedural safeguards and notice of AI interaction (Arts. 14-15). Chapter V requires risk and impact management, including testing before first use, and an assessment of moratoria or bans on certain uses (Art. 16). Each Party establishes or designates oversight mechanisms (Art. 26) and reports within two years of becoming a Party (Art. 24). Excluded: national security activities, national defence and most pre-release R&D (Art. 3(2)-(4)). The text sets no fines or penalties; disputes between Parties go to negotiation or other peaceful means (Art. 29). Entry into force follows five signatories, including three member States, consenting to be bound, plus a three-month period (Art. 30(3)).

relations.note: Art. 23(8) refers to Article 8 and Article 3 of the Statute for restricting participation in the Conference of the Parties. Art. 31(1) also cites Article 20.d of the Statute for the accession decision.

relations.target_text: European Union rules governing the matters within the scope of this Convention
relations.note: Parties that are EU members apply EU rules in their mutual relations, without prejudice to the object and purpose of the Convention. The text does not name specific EU instruments.

evidence.quote: Parties which are members of the European Union shall, in their mutual relations, apply European Union rules governing the matters within the scope of this Convention

notes: Only relations and notes are annotated here. The preamble and closing declarations are omitted from the source text. The convention states no legal basis, amendment, repeal or implementation relation. Art. 3(1)(b) leaves private-actor coverage to each Party's declaration, so the scope for private actors varies by Party. Art. 3(2) excludes national security and Art. 3(4) excludes national defence. Art. 3(3) excludes pre-release R&D unless testing could interfere with rights. Art. 27(1) allows other treaties on the same matters; these are generic and not listed. target_instrument_id is empty because the targets are not in the registry (schema requires a string).

thresholds.note: Framework convention with no size, price, scope or penalty cutoffs. Its numeric provisions are procedural: time limits (Art. 23(4), Art. 24(1), Art. 28(6), Art. 30(3)-(4), Art. 31(2), Art. 32(2)-(3), Art. 35(2)) and the entry-into-force count of five signatories including three member States (Art. 30(3)), which are not coded as thresholds under the codebook.
